text:
accent  
A variation in pronunciation that is associated with a particular region, social group, or individual.

affix  
A morpheme that is attached to another morpheme to modify its meaning, such as a prefix or suffix.

allomorph  
A variant form of a morpheme that occurs in different phonological environments.

allograph  
A phonetically different realization of the same grapheme, such as the different forms of 'a' in "cat" and "bat".

allographs  
Different phonetic forms of the same grapheme, arising from phonological variation.

allography  
The study of the different phonetic forms of a grapheme.

allophone  
A phonetic variant of a phoneme that occurs in complementary distribution.

alters  
A linguistic term not commonly used; may refer to the altered forms of linguistic features.

aspiration  
A burst of air accompanying a consonant, typically at the beginning of a word.

aspirationless  
Lacking aspiration; a characteristic of certain consonants in some languages.

asymmetry  
The lack of symmetry in the relationship between linguistic elements, such as phonemes or morphemes.

atlas  
A map that represents linguistic distribution, often showing dialect boundaries or language areas.

autosegmental  
A model of phonology that represents linguistic features on separate tiers or levels.

bilingualism  
The ability to speak and understand two or more languages fluently.

blending  
A morphological process where two words are combined into a new word by omitting some sounds.

bracketing  
The process of identifying and separating linguistic units, such as words or phrases, in a sentence.

consonant  
A speech sound produced by obstructing airflow in the vocal tract.

context  
The surrounding linguistic environment that influences the interpretation of a word or phrase.

coda  
The final part of a syllable, typically consisting of one or more consonants.

complement  
A linguistic element that completes the meaning of another element, such as a noun phrase.

complementizer  
A word or phrase that introduces a clause, such as "that" in "I think that he is here."

consonant cluster  
A sequence of two or more consonants occurring together without a vowel in between.

consonant harmony  
A phonological process in which consonants in a word are influenced by each other in terms of place or manner.

consonant mutation  
A change in the pronunciation of a consonant due to its phonological environment.

contrast  
A distinction between linguistic elements that is phonologically or grammatically significant.

contextual variation  
Changes in linguistic form or usage based on the context in which a word or phrase is used.

contour  
The pitch pattern of a tone, typically described in terms of rising, falling, or level.

convention  
A shared understanding or agreement on the use of linguistic forms or symbols.

diphthong  
A vowel sound that involves a glide from one vowel to another within the same syllable.

diphthongization  
A process in which a vowel becomes a diphthong.

discourse  
A continuous stretch of speech or writing that has a coherent theme or topic.

dissimilation  
A phonological process in which similar sounds become more different.

dissimilation  
A process where similar phonological features are changed to reduce their similarity.

diphthong  
A vowel sound that involves a glide from one vowel to another within the same syllable.

ejective consonant  
A consonant produced with a burst of air from the glottis, often found in certain languages.

ergative  
A grammatical case that marks the subject of an intransitive verb.

evidence  
Data or information used to support or refute a linguistic hypothesis.

exocentric  
Relating to a phrase
